subject: English
textbook: Pulse 2 (Form 1 & 2, KSSM) — Macmillan; Form 2 uses Units 6-9
source: DSKP KSSM Bahasa Inggeris Tingkatan 2 (CEFR-aligned, SBELC) — Bahagian Pembangunan Kurikulum, KPM (2018). Content & Learning Standards extracted from the official DSKP PDF hosted on AnyFlip (https://anyflip.com/szdx/ttnb/basic and .../51-74). VERIFICATION STATUS: CEFR target 'A2 High' = HIGH (stated in DSKP). Themes = HIGH (identical 4 themes across KSSM secondary). Content/Learning Standard codes = HIGH; exact English wording = MEDIUM (transcribed via web extraction of the DSKP; a few descriptors may need a final character-level check against the printed DSKP). Textbook = HIGH (Pulse 2, Macmillan, is the KPM-issued Form 1 & 2 text; Form 2 covers Units 6-9 per KPM Pulse 2 PdPC portal https://sites.google.com/moe-dl.edu.my/pulse2/pdpc). RPT/scheme of work = MEDIUM/LOW: RECONSTRUCTED from the 4 Form-2 Pulse 2 units + Literature component distributed across a ~40-week school year (no single official RPT PDF could be retrieved verbatim); week ordering and pacing are a reasonable teacher-editable reconstruction, not an official document.
_note_textbook_units: Pulse 2 (Macmillan) is shared across Form 1 and Form 2. Form 1 covers the Starter Unit and Units 1-5; Form 2 covers Units 6-9. A Literature in Action component (short stories, poems and a novel prescribed by KPM) runs alongside these units through the year.
_note_theme_topics: Maps each DSKP theme to the Pulse 2 (Form 2) units most relevant to it. A unit may appear under more than one theme because units often cover several themes. Teachers can edit this mapping freely.
language_focus_examples: Present perfect (with ever, never, just, already, yet)
Countable and uncountable nouns; quantifiers (some, any, much, many, a lot of)
_note_structure: Keys 'bidang' (=Skill), 'standard_kandungan' (=Content Standard) and 'standard_pembelajaran' (=Learning Standard) reuse the engine's keys. Wording follows the official DSKP KSSM English Form 2 (A2 High). Content standards that carry no Form-2 learning standard (introduced in a later form) are kept with an empty 'standard_pembelajaran' array and a note, so teachers see the full framework.

standard_kandungan._note: No Form 2 learning standard; register is introduced in a later form.

_note_rpt: RECONSTRUCTED scheme of work (RPT). Malaysian secondary school year is roughly 40 teaching weeks across two semesters, interrupted by mid-year and year-end assessments and school holidays. The four Pulse 2 Form-2 units (6-9) are each spread over about 8 weeks and integrate all skills; a Literature in Action strand and revision/assessment weeks are interleaved. Adjust dates to your school's takwim. This is NOT an official KPM RPT.

rpt.catatan: Orientation; vocabulary for jobs, chores, money and shopping.
Reading texts on earning and spending; guessing meaning from context.
Countable/uncountable nouns and quantifiers; present perfect.
Short guided text on saving/spending; punctuation and spelling.
Role-play shopping and simple suggestions.
Introduce prescribed poem/short story; characters and themes.
Consolidation and collaborative project (making a poster).
Unit 6 review and formative assessment.
Vocabulary for transport and verbs of movement.
Reading travel texts; specific details and information.
Past simple and past continuous.
Write a short account of a journey; sequence ideas.
Respond imaginatively (board game/quiz) to a text.
Talk about a memorable journey; opinions and feelings.
Collaborative project: making a tourist information leaflet.
Unit 7 review; mid-year revision begins.
Mid-year examination revision.
Mid-year examination.
Vocabulary for luck, superstitions and feelings.
Reading narratives; attitude/opinion of the writer.
First conditional; will / going to for future.
Write a short narrative; express opinions and feelings.
Connections between characters/events and pupils' own lives.
Discuss beliefs and superstitions; keep interaction going.
Consolidation and project work.
Unit 8 review and formative assessment.
Vocabulary for personal issues and health.
Reading health texts; main points and details.
Modals: should, must, have to, might (advice/obligation).
Write simple advice on staying healthy; requests and suggestions.
Imaginative response (puzzle/quiz) to a literary text.
Give and respond to advice about health and wellbeing.
Consolidation and collaborative project.
Unit 9 review and formative assessment.
Whole-text literature consolidation and creative response.
Year-end examination revision (Skills).
Year-end grammar and writing revision.
Year-end examination.
Review answers; project presentations.
Reflection, portfolio and year-end consolidation activities.
